title: hepatica asiatica subsp. insularis
intro: Hepatica asiatica subsp. insularis, commonly known as the island hepatica, is a rare and endemic subspecies of the hepatica asiatica plant, native to the Jeju Island in South Korea. It is a perennial herb that has been used in traditional medicine to treat various health conditions. The island hepatica is valued for its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties, which are attributed to its ability to lower blood sugar levels, reduce fever, and alleviate symptoms of respiratory and gastrointestinal disorders. The bioactive constituents of the island hepatica include saponins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant effects.
